prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one objectively “best” interior painting company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your needs (residential vs. commercial), budget, timeline, scope/condition of the walls, and how much prep/cleanup you want them to do. I can help you find the best fit. To start, here’s a quick guide to pick a top interior painter in St. Louis:

What to look for
- Strong local reviews (Google, Yelp) and recent photos of finished projects.  
- Proper insurance and any required business licenses.  
- Written estimate that breaks out labor, paint brand/finish, and prep (drywall repair, priming).  
- Clear warranty/guarantee on workmanship.  
- Good communication, punctuality, and a written contract with timeline and payment schedule.  
- References from recent local customers you can call.

Questions to ask every painter
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I see proof?  
- Do you provide a written estimate and contract? What’s included?  
- What brand(s) of paint and finishes do you use? Are they included in the price?  
- How much surface prep/repair is included? (e.g., sanding, priming, patching)  
- How many painters will be on site and what is the expected timeline?  
- Do you offer a warranty? How long and what does it cover?  
- Can you provide references and photos of similar jobs?

Where to start searching
- Get 3 written estimates (same scope) to compare.  
- Check BBB, Google and Yelp ratings and read a mix of good/bad reviews.  
- Consider reputable local companies and national franchises that operate locally (e.g., CertaPro Painters, Five Star Painting) plus independent St. Louis painters — but evaluate each by the criteria above.

Typical price guidance (ballpark)
- Many interior jobs range from a few hundred to a few thousand dollars. A single bedroom repainted often runs roughly $300–$1,000; whole-house jobs commonly run several thousand. Ask for square-foot or per-room pricing in the estimates so you can compare apples-to-apples.

If you want, tell me:
- ZIP code or neighborhood in St. Louis,  
- Whether it’s residential or commercial,  
- Number of rooms or square footage,  
- Any special needs (high ceilings, wallpaper removal, extensive drywall repair, desired paint brand),  

and I’ll pull together a short list of well-regarded painters to contact and draft a sample scope-of-work you can give them for estimates.
